title: Identity Concepts

header.html: Concepts of security, compliance, and identity (10–15%)

Define identity as the primary security perimeter; Define authentication; Define authorization; Describe identity providers; Describe the concept of directory services and Active Directory; Describe the concept of federation
the official SC-900 study guide, skills measured as of October 21, 2026

html:
1Identity is the new perimeter

In the past, security relied on a network perimeter: everything inside the office network was trusted. Today users, devices, apps and data are everywhere (cloud, home, mobile), so the network edge no longer protects them. Identity becomes the primary security perimeter: every request is checked by who is asking (the identity), the device and the context.

An identity can be a person (employee, customer, partner), a device, or an application or service. Each needs to prove who or what it is and be given only the access it needs.

Exam tip

. "Identity is the primary security perimeter" is the Zero Trust idea: verify identity and device for every request instead of trusting the network location.

2Authentication and authorization

Term Question Example
Authentication (AuthN) Who are you? Proving identity Password plus a code from an app
Authorization (AuthZ) What may you do? Granting permissions after sign-in Read-only access to a document library

Authentication comes first, then authorization. A person can be authenticated yet not authorized to open a resource.

Factor Meaning Examples
Something you know A secret Password, PIN
Something you have A device Phone, security key
Something you are A body trait Fingerprint, face
Exam tip

. Authentication proves identity; authorization grants rights. If a question says "proves who you are" it is authentication; "what you are allowed to do" is authorization.

3Identity providers

An identity provider (IdP) creates, maintains and manages identities and authenticates users for applications. When an app trusts an IdP, users sign in at the IdP and the app receives proof (a token).

Examples of IdPs Notes
Microsoft Entra ID The Microsoft cloud identity provider
Active Directory The traditional on-premises directory
Social providers For example sign-in with a personal account

An IdP gives single sign-on (SSO): sign in once and reach many apps.

4Directory services and Active Directory

A directory service is a central database of identities and resources (users, groups, devices) with rules for access.

Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS) Microsoft Entra ID
Where On-premises: domain controllers Cloud
Protocols Kerberos, NTLM, LDAP OAuth, SAML, OpenID Connect and HTTPS
Main use Sign-in to Windows domain resources Sign-in to cloud and web apps
Structure Domains, trees, forests, OUs, Group Policy A tenant with users, groups and apps (flat, no OUs or Group Policy)

Active Directory is Microsoft's on-premises directory service. Microsoft Entra ID is not a cloud copy of AD DS: it is a cloud identity and access management service built for web protocols.

Exam tip

. AD DS = on-premises, Kerberos and LDAP. Entra ID = cloud, OAuth and SAML. Many organizations use both (hybrid identity, module 3).

5Federation

Federation is a trust relationship between two organizations or systems so that a user who is authenticated by one can access resources of the other without a separate account.

Part Role
Identity provider Authenticates the user and issues a token
Service provider (relying party) The app that trusts the token

Federation makes SSO across organizations possible: a partner's employee signs in with their own company credentials and gets access to your app. Standards include SAML, OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect.

Exam tip

. Federation = trust between identity systems so a user needs one set of credentials. The IdP authenticates; the app trusts the IdP.

6Exam Q&A

6.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Fabrikam Outdoors staff work from home and use cloud apps. Why is the network perimeter no longer enough?

  • ACloud apps do not need sign-in because Microsoft secures every account automatically for you
  • BUsers, devices and data are outside the office network, so identity must be verified
  • CFirewalls are illegal in the cloud, so the network cannot be used for security at all
  • DIdentity only matters for administrators because ordinary users never reach sensitive data
Show the answer

Answer: B. When resources are everywhere, identity becomes the primary perimeter.

S2A user signs in with a password and a code and then opens a file. The system checks that the user has read access. Which step is the check?

  • AAuthentication
  • BFederation
  • CAuthorization
  • DHashing
Show the answer

Answer: C. Deciding what an authenticated user may do is authorization.

S3Which component creates and manages identities and authenticates users for applications?

  • AA firewall
  • BA load balancer
  • CA virtual network
  • DAn identity provider
Show the answer

Answer: D. An identity provider manages identities and authenticates users.

S4Which statement about Active Directory Domain Services is true?

  • AIt is an on-premises directory that uses Kerberos and LDAP
  • BIt is a cloud service that uses OAuth only and has no directory of users
  • CIt is a firewall that blocks traffic between two networks
  • DIt stores only encryption keys and nothing about users
Show the answer

Answer: A. AD DS is the traditional on-premises directory service.

S5A partner's employees sign in to Fabrikam's app with their own company accounts. Which concept makes this possible?

  • AFederation
  • BHashing
  • CDefense in depth
  • DObfuscation
Show the answer

Answer: A. Federation is a trust between identity systems so users can use one identity across organizations.

S6A user has a phone that receives a code. Which authentication factor is the phone?

  • ASomething you know
  • BSomething you have
  • CSomething you are
  • DSomewhere you are
Show the answer

Answer: B. A device the user possesses is a possession factor.

6.2 Recall questions

R1Why is identity called the primary security perimeter?

Show the answer

Because users, devices and data are outside the office network, so access is decided by identity.

R2What is the difference between authentication and authorization?

Show the answer

Authentication proves who you are; authorization decides what you may do.

R3What does an identity provider do?

Show the answer

Creates and manages identities and authenticates users.

R4Name the on-premises and the cloud Microsoft identity services.

Show the answer

Active Directory Domain Services and Microsoft Entra ID.

R5What is federation?

Show the answer

A trust between identity systems so one sign-in works across organizations.

R6Name the three authentication factor types.

Show the answer

Something you know, have and are.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Identity perimeter identity (person, device, app) replaces the network edge as the main boundary
AuthN vs AuthZ who you are vs what you may do; factors: know, have, are
Identity provider creates and authenticates identities; gives SSO
Directory services AD DS on-premises (Kerberos, LDAP); Entra ID cloud (OAuth, SAML, OpenID Connect)
Federation trust between identity systems; IdP authenticates, app trusts the token
